subject.title: feat: bound reads from open file descriptors

question: Should fs-safe make bounded reads from already-open descriptors a supported `advanced` contract and deliberately treat only pinned-write `fsync` `EPERM` as best effort?
rationale: Both changes are deliberate compatibility and API-policy choices rather than mechanical bug fixes; tests can validate implementation but cannot decide the library’s permanent durability and public-surface contract.

options.title: Approve the stated contract
options.body: Accept the three advanced helpers and narrowly ignore only `EPERM` from pinned-write synchronization after real behavior proof confirms the intended compatibility path.

options.title: Keep bounded reads but reject fsync relaxation
options.body: Land the allocation-bounded read work separately while preserving propagation of all fsync failures.

options.title: Defer the API shape
options.body: Pause the PR until maintainers specify whether descriptor helpers belong in the public advanced surface and what durability guarantee applies.

recommendation.title: Approve the stated contract
recommendation.body: Accept the three advanced helpers and narrowly ignore only `EPERM` from pinned-write synchronization after real behavior proof confirms the intended compatibility path.

likelyOwner.reason: The current branch and linked downstream integration provide the clearest available context for the proposed contract and compatibility behavior.
